title: Verify Important Outputs
outcome: By the end, I can verify quantities with consistent units and separate arithmetic from unsupported claims.
scenario: A fictional craft sheet calculates ribbon left after making bookmarks.
given: Four rolls each contain exactly 150 cm. Eight bookmarks use exactly 50 cm each.
No other ribbon loss is assumed; no competition result is recorded.

steps.label: Audit draft
steps.detail: “200 m remains and everyone wins” fails unit and evidence checks.

explanation: All arithmetic first uses centimetres. Converting only after subtraction avoids mixing units. The record supports available, used and remaining lengths under its no-loss assumption. It does not support a promise about winning. A numerically correct total elsewhere in a draft cannot rescue a wrong unit or an invented claim.

counterfactual.change: Make ten bookmarks instead of eight.

student_task: Correct the draft and identify which part needs another source rather than a calculation.
teacher_answer: It should say 200 cm or 2 m remains. Winning needs genuine result evidence; remove the unsupported promise.
project_evidence: Check sorter calculations with explicit units and verify explanation claims against their actual catalogue evidence.
limits: Real cutting losses or inaccurate roll lengths would change this toy calculation; the assumption must be declared.
review_note: Individually reviewed fictional topic example; arithmetic and declared policies checked. This is supported practice, not the reserved independent assessment.

mini_visual.title: Ribbon quantities in one consistent unit
